LECTURE 14 Stage 3: Attention

Self-Attention Mechanism

How Query, Key, and Value projections transform simple attention into the powerful self-attention mechanism at the heart of every Transformer
50 min read Hands-on coding Intermediate-Advanced

From Simple Attention to Self-Attention

In Lecture 13, we implemented dot-product attention using raw embeddings as both the query and key vectors. While this works, it has a fundamental limitation: each token's embedding must simultaneously serve as the "question" it asks, the "answer" it provides to others, and the "information" it carries. That is too many roles for a single vector.

Self-attention solves this by introducing three separate learned projections that transform each token's embedding into three distinct roles:

  • Query (Q): "What am I looking for?" — represents what information this token needs
  • Key (K): "What do I contain?" — represents what information this token offers
  • Value (V): "What information do I actually provide?" — the content that gets aggregated
Analogy: The Library Search

Imagine a library where every book has a catalog card (Key) describing its contents and the actual book contents (Value). When you walk in with a research question (Query), you compare your question against every catalog card. The cards that match best tell you which books to read. You then read a weighted mixture of those books proportional to how well their catalog cards matched your question. Self-attention works identically — the Query, Key, and Value are just different "views" of each token, learned to serve these specific roles.

The QKV Transformation Matrices

Each input embedding x of dimension d_model is projected through three weight matrices to produce the Query, Key, and Value vectors:

Q = x @ W_q # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
K = x @ W_k # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
V = x @ W_v # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_v) -> (d_v,)

Where:

  • W_q: Query weight matrix of shape (d_model, d_k)
  • W_k: Key weight matrix of shape (d_model, d_k)
  • W_v: Value weight matrix of shape (d_model, d_v)

Typically, d_k = d_v = d_model for single-head attention (we will see different choices with multi-head attention later). These weight matrices are learned parameters — the model adjusts them during training to discover what projections are most useful for the task.

Key Insight: The projection matrices are the "learnable" part of self-attention. They allow the model to learn different similarity functions for different types of relationships. One attention head might learn to focus on syntactic structure (subject-verb agreement), while another learns semantic relationships (word meaning similarity). The raw embedding cannot do this because it is a single, fixed representation.

Why Three Separate Projections?

A natural question is: why not just use the raw embeddings for everything? The answer lies in the asymmetry of attention relationships.

Consider the sentence: "The animal did not cross the street because it was too tired." When processing "it," the model needs to determine that "it" refers to "animal" (not "street"). The query for "it" needs to encode "I am a pronoun looking for my antecedent," while the key for "animal" needs to encode "I am a noun that could be an antecedent." These are very different roles that require different projections of the same embedding space.

Furthermore, what "animal" provides when attended to (its Value) might be different from how it advertises itself (its Key). The Value might carry rich semantic content about animals, while the Key only needs to signal "I am a singular, animate noun."

Python
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

# --- QKV Projection Matrices from Scratch ---

# Configuration
d_model = 8 # embedding dimension
d_k = 6 # query/key dimension
d_v = 6 # value dimension
n_tokens = 5

tokens = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "mat"]

# Random input embeddings (in practice, these come from the embedding layer)
X = np.random.randn(n_tokens, d_model)

# Initialize QKV weight matrices (in practice, learned via training)
# Using Xavier/Glorot initialization
scale_init = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))
W_q = np.random.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale_init
W_k = np.random.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale_init
W_v = np.random.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale_init

print("=== QKV Projections ===\
")
print("Input X shape: {} (n_tokens x d_model)".format(X.shape))
print("W_q shape: {} (d_model x d_k)".format(W_q.shape))
print("W_k shape: {} (d_model x d_k)".format(W_k.shape))
print("W_v shape: {} (d_model x d_v)".format(W_v.shape))

# Project all tokens at once (matrix multiplication)
Q = X @ W_q # (n_tokens, d_k)
K = X @ W_k # (n_tokens, d_k)
V = X @ W_v # (n_tokens, d_v)

print("\
Q shape: {} (queries)".format(Q.shape))
print("K shape: {} (keys)".format(K.shape))
print("V shape: {} (values)".format(V.shape))

# Show how different projections create different representations
print("\
--- Same token, different projections ---")
for i, tok in enumerate(tokens):
 q_norm = np.linalg.norm(Q[i])
 k_norm = np.linalg.norm(K[i])
 v_norm = np.linalg.norm(V[i])
 # How different are Q and K for the same token?
 qk_cos = np.dot(Q[i], K[i][:d_k]) / (q_norm * k_norm + 1e-8)
 print(" '{}': |Q|={:.2f}, |K|={:.2f}, |V|={:.2f}, cos(Q,K)={:.3f}".format(
 tok, q_norm, k_norm, v_norm, qk_cos))

print("\
Notice: Q and K for the same token are NOT identical!")
print("The projections learn different 'views' of each token.")
print("cos(Q,K) varies per token - they encode different aspects.")

Computing Self-Attention Step by Step

Now let us combine the QKV projections with the dot-product attention mechanism from Lecture 13. The complete self-attention computation is:

  1. Project inputs through W_q, W_k, W_v to get Q, K, V matrices
  2. Compute attention scores: Q multiplied by K-transpose
  3. Scale by sqrt(d_k)
  4. Apply softmax to get attention weights
  5. Multiply weights by V to get the output

In matrix notation, the famous attention formula:

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V

This single line is one of the most consequential equations in modern AI. Let us unpack it with code.

Python
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 """Numerically stable softmax."""
 e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True))
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)


class SingleHeadSelfAttention:
 """
 Single-head self-attention mechanism implemented from scratch.

 This is the fundamental building block of the Transformer.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, d_k, d_v, seed=42):
 """
 Args:
 d_model: Input embedding dimension
 d_k: Query/Key projection dimension
 d_v: Value projection dimension
 """
 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))

 self.d_k = d_k
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale

 def forward(self, X):
 """
 Compute self-attention.

 Args:
 X: Input tensor of shape (seq_len, d_model)

 Returns:
 output: Attention output of shape (seq_len, d_v)
 weights: Attention weights of shape (seq_len, seq_len)
 """
 # Step 1: Project to Q, K, V
 Q = X @ self.W_q # (seq_len, d_k)
 K = X @ self.W_k # (seq_len, d_k)
 V = X @ self.W_v # (seq_len, d_v)

 # Step 2: Compute scaled dot-product scores
 scores = Q @ K.T # (seq_len, seq_len)
 scores = scores / np.sqrt(self.d_k)

 # Step 3: Softmax
 weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1) # (seq_len, seq_len)

 # Step 4: Weighted sum of values
 output = weights @ V # (seq_len, d_v)

 return output, weights


# --- Test the implementation ---
tokens = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]
n_tokens = len(tokens)
d_model = 16
d_k = 12
d_v = 12

# Input embeddings
np.random.seed(7)
X = np.random.randn(n_tokens, d_model)

# Create and run self-attention
attn = SingleHeadSelfAttention(d_model, d_k, d_v, seed=42)
output, weights = attn.forward(X)

print("=== Single-Head Self-Attention ===\
")
print("Input shape: {}".format(X.shape))
print("Output shape: {}".format(output.shape))
print("Weights shape: {}\
".format(weights.shape))

# Display attention weights
print("--- Attention Weight Matrix ---")
header = " "
for tok in tokens:
 header += "{:>7s}".format(tok[:6])
print(header)
print(" " + "-------" * n_tokens)

for i in range(n_tokens):
 row = "{:>7s} | ".format(tokens[i])
 for j in range(n_tokens):
 w = weights[i][j]
 if w > 0.25:
 row += " {:.3f}".format(w)
 elif w > 0.10:
 row += " {:.3f}".format(w)
 else:
 row += " .{:02d} ".format(int(w * 100))
 print(row)

# Verify properties
print("\
--- Verification ---")
print("All weights positive:", np.all(weights >= 0))
print("Rows sum to 1:", np.allclose(weights.sum(axis=1), 1.0))
print("Output is different from input (projected):", not np.allclose(output, X[:, :d_v]))

# Show how output blends information
print("\
--- How Self-Attention Blends Information ---")
print("For token 'cat' (index 1):")
print(" Output is a weighted blend of all Value vectors:")
for j in range(n_tokens):
 print(" {:.1f}% from '{}'".format(weights[1][j]*100, tokens[j]))
print(" Strongest attention: '{}'".format(tokens[np.argmax(weights[1])]))

Understanding What Q, K, V Learn to Represent

During training, the weight matrices W_q, W_k, and W_v are optimized through gradient descent. But what do they actually learn?

Queries: "What Am I Looking For?"

The query projection learns to transform each token into a representation of what information that token needs from the context. For example, a verb's query might encode "I need a subject" or "I need an object," while a pronoun's query might encode "I need my antecedent."

Keys: "What Do I Offer?"

The key projection learns to create a "searchable label" for each token — a representation of what information that token can provide. A noun's key might encode "I am a subject candidate" or "I carry entity information."

Values: "What Content Do I Carry?"

The value projection determines what information actually gets passed when a token is attended to. This is often richer and more detailed than the key. While the key says "I have semantic content about animals," the value carries the actual semantic features.

Pro Tip: A useful mental model is that Q and K determine the routing (who talks to whom), while V determines the content (what gets transmitted). This separation of routing and content is one of the key innovations that makes Transformers so powerful. It is similar to how a postal system works: the address (Key-Query matching) determines where a letter goes, but the address is separate from the letter's contents (Value).

Attention Patterns: What the Model Learns

Trained Transformer models develop remarkably interpretable attention patterns. Research has identified several common patterns that different attention heads learn:

Positional Attention

Some heads learn to attend to nearby tokens (local context), the previous token, or the next token. These capture local syntactic patterns.

Syntactic Attention

Some heads learn grammatical relationships: subjects attend to their verbs, adjectives attend to the nouns they modify.

Coreference Attention

Some heads specialize in resolving pronouns to their antecedents: "it" attends strongly to the noun it refers to.

Semantic Attention

Some heads attend to semantically related words regardless of position, capturing topic and meaning relationships.

Let us visualize different types of attention patterns that might emerge during training.

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True))
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)

# --- Visualizing Different Attention Patterns ---
tokens = ["The", "cat", "sat", "on", "the", "mat"]
n = len(tokens)

print("=== Common Attention Patterns in Trained Models ===\
")

# Pattern 1: "Previous token" attention

print("(Some heads learn to simply look at the preceding token)")
prev_scores = np.full((n, n), -10.0)
for i in range(n):

for i in range(n):

# Pattern 2: "Syntactic" attention (subject-verb, det-noun)
print("\
--- Pattern 2: Syntactic Attention ---")
print("(Captures grammatical relationships)")
syn_scores = np.full((n, n), -5.0)
# "The" -> "cat" (determiner-noun)
syn_scores[0, 1] = 4.0
# "cat" -> "sat" (subject-verb)
syn_scores[1, 2] = 4.0

syn_scores[2, 1] = 4.0
# "the" -> "mat" (determiner-noun)
syn_scores[4, 5] = 4.0
# "on" -> "mat" (preposition-object)
syn_scores[3, 5] = 3.0

--- Pattern 3: Global / Aggregate Attention ---")

# Every token attends roughly uniformly

print("DIFFERENT patterns, each capturing a different type")
print("of relationship. This is why multi-head attention")
print("(which we cover in a later lecture) is so powerful!")

The Self-Attention Computation Graph

Let us trace through the dimensions at each step of self-attention to build a complete mental model. Assume we have a sequence of T tokens with embedding dimension d_model:

Step Operation Input Shape Output Shape
1 Q = X @ W_q (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
2 K = X @ W_k (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
3 V = X @ W_v (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_v) (T, d_v)
4 scores = Q @ K.T (T, d_k) @ (d_k, T) (T, T)
5 scores / sqrt(d_k) (T, T) (T, T)
6 weights = softmax(scores) (T, T) (T, T)
7 output = weights @ V (T, T) @ (T, d_v) (T, d_v)
Important: The attention weight matrix at Step 6 is a (T, T) matrix. For a sequence of 1000 tokens, this is a million-element matrix. For 4096 tokens, it is nearly 17 million elements. This quadratic scaling with sequence length is the primary computational bottleneck of Transformer attention, and the reason why much research has gone into efficient attention variants.

Self-Attention vs. Simple Attention

To solidify understanding, let us directly compare what happens with raw embeddings (Lecture 13 approach) versus with learned QKV projections (self-attention):

Python
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True))
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)


tokens = ["The", "animal", "did", "not", "cross", "it"]
n = len(tokens)
d_model = 16
d_k = 12

# Input embeddings
X = np.random.randn(n, d_model)

print("=== Simple Attention vs Self-Attention ===\
")

# --- Simple attention (no projections) ---
raw_scores = X @ X.T / np.sqrt(d_model)
raw_weights = softmax(raw_scores)

print("--- Simple Attention (raw embeddings) ---")
print("Score = X @ X.T / sqrt(d_model)")
print("Focus on 'it' (idx 5) attending to other tokens:")
for j in range(n):
 bar = "|" + "=" * int(raw_weights[5][j] * 40)
 print(" '{:>6s}': {:.4f} {}".format(tokens[j], raw_weights[5][j], bar))

# --- Self-attention (with projections) ---
rng = np.random.RandomState(99)
scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))
W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale

Q = X @ W_q
K = X @ W_k
V = X @ W_v

proj_scores = Q @ K.T / np.sqrt(d_k)
proj_weights = softmax(proj_scores)

print("\
--- Self-Attention (with QKV projections) ---")
print("Q = X @ W_q, K = X @ W_k")
print("Score = Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)")
print("Focus on 'it' (idx 5) attending to other tokens:")
for j in range(n):
 bar = "|" + "=" * int(proj_weights[5][j] * 40)
 print(" '{:>6s}': {:.4f} {}".format(tokens[j], proj_weights[5][j], bar))

# Show how different W matrices create different patterns
print("\
--- Different Projections = Different Patterns ---")
print("Using 3 different sets of W_q, W_k:")
for trial in range(3):
 rng2 = np.random.RandomState(trial * 100 + 1)
 W_q2 = rng2.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 W_k2 = rng2.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 Q2 = X @ W_q2
 K2 = X @ W_k2
 w2 = softmax(Q2 @ K2.T / np.sqrt(d_k))
 top_idx = np.argmax(w2[5])
 print(" Set {}: 'it' attends most to '{}' ({:.1f}%)".format(
 trial + 1, tokens[top_idx], w2[5][top_idx] * 100))

print("\
Key insight: The projection matrices control WHAT the model")
print("attends to. Different projections create different attention")
print("patterns from the SAME input embeddings. Training optimizes")
print("these projections to capture useful relationships.")

Parameter Count and Computational Cost

Let us quantify the resources self-attention requires:

  • Parameters: Three weight matrices, each of size (d_model x d_k), totaling 3 * d_model * d_k parameters. For GPT-2 with d_model = 768 and d_k = 64 per head, that is 3 * 768 * 64 = 147,456 parameters per head.
  • Computation: The dominant cost is the (T, T) attention matrix. For sequence length T and d_k dimensions, this is O(T^2 * d_k) operations.
  • Memory: Storing the full (T, T) attention matrix requires O(T^2) memory.

This quadratic scaling is why standard Transformers struggle with very long sequences and why techniques like FlashAttention, sparse attention, and linear attention have been developed.

Key Takeaways

  • Three projections, three roles: The Query asks "what do I need?", the Key advertises "what do I have?", and the Value carries "what I will give you." Separating these roles is essential.
  • Learned projections enable flexible attention: Different weight matrices W_q, W_k, W_v can learn to capture different types of relationships (syntactic, semantic, positional) from the same input.
  • The attention formula: softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V computes attention in a single elegant expression that is fully differentiable and GPU-friendly.
  • Quadratic complexity: The T x T attention matrix means computational and memory costs grow quadratically with sequence length — the primary bottleneck of Transformer models.
  • Interpretable patterns emerge: Trained attention heads develop distinct, often interpretable specializations (syntactic parsing, coreference resolution, positional attention).

LECȚIA 14 Etapa 3: Atenție

Mecanismul de atenție proprie (Self-Attention)

Cum proiecțiile Query, Key și Value transformă atenția simplă în puternicul mecanism de atenție proprie din inima fiecărui Transformer
50 min lectură Exerciții practice de cod Intermediar-Avansat

De la atenția simplă la atenția proprie

În Lecția 13, am implementat atenția cu produs scalar folosind embedding-urile brute atât ca vectori de interogare, cât și ca vectori cheie. Deși funcționează, are o limitare fundamentală: embedding-ul fiecărui token trebuie să servească simultan ca „întrebarea” pe care o pune, ca „răspunsul” pe care îl oferă altora și ca „informația” pe care o conține. Sunt prea multe roluri pentru un singur vector.

Atenția proprie rezolvă aceasta prin introducerea a trei proiecții separate învățate care transformă embedding-ul fiecărui token în trei roluri distincte:

  • Query (Q): „Ce caut?” — reprezintă ce informație are nevoie acest token
  • Key (K): „Ce conțin?” — reprezintă ce informație oferă acest token
  • Value (V): „Ce informație furnizez de fapt?” — conținutul care este agregat
Analogie: Căutarea în bibliotecă

Imaginați-vă o bibliotecă unde fiecare carte are o fișă de catalog (Key) care descrie conținutul său și conținutul propriu-zis al cărții (Value). Când intrați cu o întrebare de cercetare (Query), comparați întrebarea dvs. cu fiecare fișă de catalog. Fișele care se potrivesc cel mai bine vă indică ce cărți să citiți. Apoi citiți un amestec ponderat al acelor cărți proporțional cu cât de bine s-au potrivit fișele de catalog cu întrebarea dvs. Atenția proprie funcționează identic — Query, Key și Value sunt doar „perspective” diferite ale fiecărui token, învățate să servească aceste roluri specifice.

Matricele de transformare QKV

Fiecare embedding de intrare x de dimensiune d_model este proiectat prin trei matrice de ponderi pentru a produce vectorii Query, Key și Value:

Q = x @ W_q # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
K = x @ W_k # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
V = x @ W_v # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_v) -> (d_v,)

Unde:

  • W_q: Matricea de ponderi Query de forma (d_model, d_k)
  • W_k: Matricea de ponderi Key de forma (d_model, d_k)
  • W_v: Matricea de ponderi Value de forma (d_model, d_v)

De obicei, d_k = d_v = d_model pentru atenția cu un singur cap (vom vedea alegeri diferite cu atenția multi-cap mai târziu). Aceste matrice de ponderi sunt parametri învățați — modelul le ajustează în timpul antrenamentului pentru a descoperi ce proiecții sunt cele mai utile pentru sarcină.

Ideea cheie: Matricele de proiecție sunt partea „învățabilă” a atenției proprii. Permit modelului să învețe funcții de similaritate diferite pentru diferite tipuri de relații. Un cap de atenție ar putea învăța să se concentreze pe structura sintactică (acordul subiect-verb), în timp ce altul învață relații semantice (similaritatea semnificației cuvintelor). Embedding-ul brut nu poate face acest lucru pentru că este o singură reprezentare fixă.

De ce trei proiecții separate?

O întrebare naturală este: de ce nu folosim pur și simplu embedding-urile brute pentru totul? Răspunsul stă în asimetria relațiilor de atenție.

Considerați propoziția: „The animal did not cross the street because it was too tired.” Când procesează „it”, modelul trebuie să determine că „it” se referă la „animal” (nu la „street”). Interogarea pentru „it” trebuie să codifice „sunt un pronume care își caută antecedentul”, în timp ce cheia pentru „animal” trebuie să codifice „sunt un substantiv care ar putea fi un antecedent”. Acestea sunt roluri foarte diferite care necesită proiecții diferite ale aceluiași spațiu de embedding.

Mai mult, ceea ce „animal” furnizează când i se acordă atenție (Value-ul său) ar putea fi diferit de modul în care se anunță (Key-ul său). Value-ul ar putea conține informații semantice bogate despre animale, în timp ce Key-ul trebuie doar să semnaleze „sunt un substantiv singular, animat”.

Acum să combinăm proiecțiile QKV cu mecanismul de atenție prin produs scalar din Lecția 13. Calculul complet al atenției proprii este:

  1. Proiectarea intrărilor prin W_q, W_k, W_v pentru a obține matricele Q, K, V
  2. Calcularea scorurilor de atenție: Q multiplicat cu K-transpus
  3. Scalarea cu sqrt(d_k)
  4. Aplicarea softmax pentru a obține ponderile de atenție
  5. Multiplicarea ponderilor cu V pentru a obține ieșirea

În notație matricială, faimoasa formulă de atenție:

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V

class SingleHeadSelfAttention:
 """
 Single-head self-attention mechanism implemented from scratch.

 This is the fundamental building block of the Transformer.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, d_k, d_v, seed=42):
 """
 Args:
 d_model: Input embedding dimension
 d_k: Query/Key projection dimension
 d_v: Value projection dimension
 """
 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))

 self.d_k = d_k
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale

 def forward(self, X):
 """
 Compute self-attention.

 Args:
 X: Input tensor of shape (seq_len, d_model)

 Returns:
 output: Attention output of shape (seq_len, d_v)
 weights: Attention weights of shape (seq_len, seq_len)
 """
 # Step 1: Project to Q, K, V
 Q = X @ self.W_q # (seq_len, d_k)
 K = X @ self.W_k # (seq_len, d_k)
 V = X @ self.W_v # (seq_len, d_v)

 # Step 2: Compute scaled dot-product scores
 scores = Q @ K.T # (seq_len, seq_len)
 scores = scores / np.sqrt(self.d_k)

 # Step 3: Softmax
 weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1) # (seq_len, seq_len)

 # Step 4: Weighted sum of values
 output = weights @ V # (seq_len, d_v)

 return output, weights

Înțelegerea a ce învață Q, K, V să reprezinte

În timpul antrenamentului, matricele de ponderi W_q, W_k și W_v sunt optimizate prin coborârea gradientului. Dar ce învață de fapt?

Interogări (Queries): „Ce caut?”

Proiecția de interogare învață să transforme fiecare token într-o reprezentare a ce informație are nevoie acel token din context. De exemplu, interogarea unui verb ar putea codifica „am nevoie de un subiect” sau „am nevoie de un obiect”, în timp ce interogarea unui pronume ar putea codifica „am nevoie de antecedentul meu”.

Chei (Keys): „Ce ofer?”

Proiecția de cheie învață să creeze o „etichetă de căutare” pentru fiecare token — o reprezentare a ce informație poate furniza acel token. Cheia unui substantiv ar putea codifica „sunt un candidat de subiect” sau „conțin informații despre entități”.

Valori (Values): „Ce conținut transport?”

Proiecția de valoare determină ce informație este transmisă efectiv când unui token i se acordă atenție. Aceasta este adesea mai bogată și mai detaliată decât cheia. În timp ce cheia spune „am conținut semantic despre animale”, valoarea conține trăsăturile semantice efective.

Sfat pro: Un model mental util este că Q și K determină rutarea (cine vorbește cu cine), în timp ce V determină conținutul (ce se transmite). Această separare a rutării și conținutului este una dintre inovațiile cheie care fac Transformer-ele atât de puternice. Este similar cu modul în care funcționează un sistem poștal: adresa (potrivirea Key-Query) determină unde ajunge o scrisoare, dar adresa este separată de conținutul scrisorii (Value).

Atenție pozițională

Unele capete învață să acorde atenție token-urilor apropiate (context local), token-ului precedent sau următorului token. Acestea surprind modele sintactice locale.

Atenție sintactică

Unele capete învață relații gramaticale: subiectele acordă atenție verbelor lor, adjectivele acordă atenție substantivelor pe care le modifică.

Atenție de coreferință

Unele capete se specializează în rezolvarea pronumelor către antecedenții lor: „it” acordă atenție puternică substantivului la care se referă.

Atenție semantică

Unele capete acordă atenție cuvintelor înrudite semantic indiferent de poziție, surprinzând relații de subiect și semnificație.

Numărul de parametri și costul computațional

Să cuantificăm resursele pe care le necesită atenția proprie:

  • Parametri: Trei matrice de ponderi, fiecare de dimensiune (d_model x d_k), totalizând 3 * d_model * d_k parametri. Pentru GPT-2 cu d_model = 768 și d_k = 64 per cap, aceasta înseamnă 3 * 768 * 64 = 147.456 parametri per cap.
  • Calcul: Costul dominant este matricea de atenție (T, T). Pentru lungimea secvenței T și d_k dimensiuni, aceasta este O(T^2 * d_k) operații.
  • Memorie: Stocarea matricei complete de atenție (T, T) necesită O(T^2) memorie.

Această scalare pătratică este motivul pentru care Transformer-ele standard se luptă cu secvențe foarte lungi și de ce s-au dezvoltat tehnici precum FlashAttention, atenția rară și atenția liniară.

  • Proiecțiile învățate permit atenție flexibilă: Diferite matrice de ponderi W_q, W_k, W_v pot învăța să surprindă diferite tipuri de relații (sintactice, semantice, poziționale) din aceeași intrare.

  • Modele interpretabile apar: Capetele de atenție antrenate dezvoltă specializări distincte, adesea interpretabile (analiză sintactică, rezolvarea coreferinței, atenție pozițională).

Αυτοι ειναι πολλοι ρολοι για ενα μονο διανυσμα.

Το self-attention λυνει αυτο το προβλημα εισαγοντας τρεις ξεχωριστες εκπαιδευμενες προβολες που μετασχηματιζουν το embedding καθε token σε τρεις διακριτους ρολους:

  • Key (K): «Τι περιεχω;» — αναπαριστα ποια πληροφορια προσφερει αυτο το token
  • Value (V): «Τι πληροφορια παρεχω πραγματικα;» — το περιεχομενο που συγκεντρωνεται
Αναλογια: Η Αναζητηση στη Βιβλιοθηκη

Φανταστειτε μια βιβλιοθηκη οπου καθε βιβλιο εχει μια καρτα καταλογου (Key) που περιγραφει το περιεχομενο του και το πραγματικο περιεχομενο του βιβλιου (Value). Οταν μπαινετε με ενα ερευνητικο ερωτημα (Query), συγκρινετε το ερωτημα σας με καθε καρτα καταλογου. Οι καρτες που ταιριαζουν καλυτερα σας λενε ποια βιβλια να διαβασετε. Στη συνεχεια διαβαζετε ενα σταθμισμενο μειγμα αυτων των βιβλιων αναλογα με το ποσο καλα ταιριαζαν οι καρτες καταλογου τους με το ερωτημα σας. Το self-attention λειτουργει πανομοιοτυπα — τα Query, Key και Value ειναι απλα διαφορετικες «οπτικες γωνιες» καθε token, εκπαιδευμενες για να εξυπηρετουν αυτους τους συγκεκριμενους ρολους.

Οι Πινακες Μετασχηματισμου QKV

Καθε embedding εισοδου x διαστασης d_model προβαλλεται μεσω τριων πινακων βαρων για να παραχθουν τα διανυσματα Query, Key και Value:

Q = x @ W_q # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
K = x @ W_k # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
V = x @ W_v # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_v) -> (d_v,)

Οπου:

  • W_q: Πινακας βαρων Query με σχημα (d_model, d_k)
  • W_k: Πινακας βαρων Key με σχημα (d_model, d_k)
  • W_v: Πινακας βαρων Value με σχημα (d_model, d_v)

Συνηθως, d_k = d_v = d_model για προσοχη μονου κεφαλιου (θα δουμε διαφορετικες επιλογες με την προσοχη πολλαπλων κεφαλων αργοτερα). Αυτοι οι πινακες βαρων ειναι εκπαιδευμενες παραμετροι — το μοντελο τις προσαρμοζει κατα την εκπαιδευση για να ανακαλυψει ποιες προβολες ειναι πιο χρησιμες για την εργασια.

Βασικη Διαπιστωση: Οι πινακες προβολης ειναι το «εκπαιδευσιμο» μερος του self-attention. Επιτρεπουν στο μοντελο να μαθει διαφορετικες συναρτησεις ομοιοτητας για διαφορετικους τυπους σχεσεων. Το ακατεργαστο embedding δεν μπορει να το κανει αυτο γιατι ειναι μια μοναδικη, σταθερη αναπαρασταση.

Γιατι Τρεις Ξεχωριστες Προβολες;

Ενα φυσικο ερωτημα ειναι: γιατι να μην χρησιμοποιουμε απλα τα ακατεργαστα embeddings για τα παντα; Η απαντηση βρισκεται στην ασυμμετρια των σχεσεων προσοχης.

Σκεφτειτε την προταση: «The animal did not cross the street because it was too tired.» Οταν επεξεργαζεται το «it», το μοντελο πρεπει να προσδιορισει οτι το «it» αναφερεται στο «animal» (οχι στο «street»). Το query για το «it» πρεπει να κωδικοποιει το «ειμαι αντωνυμια που ψαχνει το αντικειμενο αναφορας της», ενω το key για το «animal» πρεπει να κωδικοποιει το «ειμαι ουσιαστικο που θα μπορουσε να ειναι αντικειμενο αναφορας». Αυτοι ειναι πολυ διαφορετικοι ρολοι που απαιτουν διαφορετικες προβολες του ιδιου χωρου embeddings.

Επιπλεον, αυτο που παρεχει το «animal» οταν λαμβανει προσοχη (το Value του) μπορει να ειναι διαφορετικο απο το πως διαφημιζει τον εαυτο του (το Key του). Το Value μπορει να μεταφερει πλουσιο σημασιολογικο περιεχομενο για ζωα, ενω το Key χρειαζεται μονο να σηματοδοτει «ειμαι ενικο, εμψυχο ουσιαστικο».

class SingleHeadSelfAttention:
 """
 Single-head self-attention mechanism implemented from scratch.

 This is the fundamental building block of the Transformer.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, d_k, d_v, seed=42):
 """
 Args:
 d_model: Input embedding dimension
 d_k: Query/Key projection dimension
 d_v: Value projection dimension
 """
 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))

 self.d_k = d_k
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale

 def forward(self, X):
 """
 Compute self-attention.

 Args:
 X: Input tensor of shape (seq_len, d_model)

 Returns:
 output: Attention output of shape (seq_len, d_v)
 weights: Attention weights of shape (seq_len, seq_len)
 """
 # Step 1: Project to Q, K, V
 Q = X @ self.W_q # (seq_len, d_k)
 K = X @ self.W_k # (seq_len, d_k)
 V = X @ self.W_v # (seq_len, d_v)

 # Step 2: Compute scaled dot-product scores
 scores = Q @ K.T # (seq_len, seq_len)
 scores = scores / np.sqrt(self.d_k)

 # Step 3: Softmax
 weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1) # (seq_len, seq_len)

 # Step 4: Weighted sum of values
 output = weights @ V # (seq_len, d_v)

 return output, weights

Κατα την εκπαιδευση, οι πινακες βαρων W_q, W_k και W_v βελτιστοποιουνται μεσω καθοδου κλισης. Αλλα τι μαθαινουν πραγματικα;

Queries: «Τι Ψαχνω;»

Η προβολη query μαθαινει να μετασχηματιζει καθε token σε μια αναπαρασταση του ποια πληροφορια χρειαζεται αυτο το token απο το συγκειμενο. Για παραδειγμα, το query ενος ρηματος μπορει να κωδικοποιει το «χρειαζομαι υποκειμενο» η «χρειαζομαι αντικειμενο», ενω το query μιας αντωνυμιας μπορει να κωδικοποιει το «χρειαζομαι το αντικειμενο αναφορας μου».

Keys: «Τι Προσφερω;»

Η προβολη key μαθαινει να δημιουργει μια «αναζητησιμη ετικετα» για καθε token — μια αναπαρασταση του ποια πληροφορια μπορει να παρεχει αυτο το token. Το key ενος ουσιαστικου μπορει να κωδικοποιει το «ειμαι υποψηφιο υποκειμενο» η «μεταφερω πληροφορια οντοτητας».

Values: «Τι Περιεχομενο Μεταφερω;»

Η προβολη value καθοριζει ποια πληροφορια περναει πραγματικα οταν ενα token λαμβανει προσοχη. Αυτη ειναι συχνα πλουσιοτερη και πιο λεπτομερης απο το key. Ενω το key λεει «εχω σημασιολογικο περιεχομενο για ζωα», το value μεταφερει τα πραγματικα σημασιολογικα χαρακτηριστικα.

Συμβουλη: Ενα χρησιμο νοητικο μοντελο ειναι οτι τα Q και K καθοριζουν τη δρομολογηση (ποιος μιλαει σε ποιον), ενω το V καθοριζει το περιεχομενο (τι μεταδιδεται). Αυτος ο διαχωρισμος δρομολογησης και περιεχομενου ειναι μια απο τις βασικες καινοτομιες που κανουν τους Transformers τοσο ισχυρους. Ειναι παρομοιο με το πως λειτουργει ενα ταχυδρομικο συστημα: η διευθυνση (αντιστοιχια Key-Query) καθοριζει που πηγαινει ενα γραμμα, αλλα η διευθυνση ειναι ξεχωριστη απο το περιεχομενο του γραμματος (Value).

Προτυπα Προσοχης: Τι Μαθαινει το Μοντελο

Τα εκπαιδευμενα μοντελα Transformer αναπτυσσουν εντυπωσιακα ερμηνευσιμα προτυπα προσοχης. Η ερευνα εχει εντοπισει αρκετα συνηθισμενα προτυπα που μαθαινουν διαφορετικα κεφαλια προσοχης:

Προσοχη Θεσης

Καποια κεφαλια μαθαινουν να εστιαζουν σε κοντινα tokens (τοπικο συγκειμενο), στο προηγουμενο token η στο επομενο token. Αυτα συλλαμβανουν τοπικα συντακτικα προτυπα.

Συντακτικη Προσοχη

Καποια κεφαλια μαθαινουν γραμματικες σχεσεις: τα υποκειμενα εστιαζουν στα ρηματα τους, τα επιθετα εστιαζουν στα ουσιαστικα που τροποποιουν.

Προσοχη Συναναφορας

Καποια κεφαλια εξειδικευονται στην επιλυση αντωνυμιων στα αντικειμενα αναφορας τους: το «it» εστιαζει εντονα στο ουσιαστικο στο οποιο αναφερεται.

Σημασιολογικη Προσοχη

Καποια κεφαλια εστιαζουν σε σημασιολογικα σχετικες λεξεις ανεξαρτητα θεσης, συλλαμβανοντας σχεσεις θεματος και νοηματος.

Ας ακολουθησουμε τις διαστασεις σε καθε βημα του self-attention για να χτισουμε ενα πληρες νοητικο μοντελο. Υποθετουμε οτι εχουμε μια ακολουθια T tokens με διασταση embedding d_model:

Βημα Λειτουργια Σχημα Εισοδου Σχημα Εξοδου
1 Q = X @ W_q (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)

4 scores = Q @ K.T (T, d_k) @ (d_k, T) (T, T)
5 scores / sqrt(d_k) (T, T) (T, T)
6 weights = softmax(scores) (T, T) (T, T)
7 output = weights @ V (T, T) @ (T, d_v) (T, d_v)

Das funktioniert zwar, hat aber eine grundlegende Einschränkung: Das Embedding jedes Tokens muss gleichzeitig als die „Frage" dienen, die es stellt, als die „Antwort", die es anderen liefert, und als die „Information", die es trägt. Das sind zu viele Rollen für einen einzigen Vektor.

Self-Attention löst dieses Problem, indem drei separate gelernte Projektionen eingeführt werden, die das Embedding jedes Tokens in drei unterschiedliche Rollen verwandeln:

  • Query (Q): „Wonach suche ich?" — repräsentiert, welche Information dieses Token benötigt
  • Key (K): „Was enthalte ich?" — repräsentiert, welche Information dieses Token anbietet
  • Value (V): „Welche Information liefere ich tatsächlich?" — der Inhalt, der aggregiert wird
Analogie: Die Bibliothekssuche

Stellen Sie sich eine Bibliothek vor, in der jedes Buch eine Katalogkarte (Key) besitzt, die seinen Inhalt beschreibt, sowie den eigentlichen Buchinhalt (Value). Wenn Sie mit einer Forschungsfrage (Query) hereinkommen, vergleichen Sie Ihre Frage mit jeder Katalogkarte. Die Karten, die am besten passen, zeigen Ihnen, welche Bücher Sie lesen sollten. Anschließend lesen Sie eine gewichtete Mischung dieser Bücher, proportional dazu, wie gut ihre Katalogkarten zu Ihrer Frage passten. Self-Attention funktioniert identisch — Query, Key und Value sind lediglich unterschiedliche „Ansichten" jedes Tokens, die darauf trainiert wurden, diese spezifischen Rollen zu erfüllen.

Die QKV-Transformationsmatrizen

Jedes Eingabe-Embedding x der Dimension d_model wird durch drei Gewichtsmatrizen projiziert, um die Query-, Key- und Value-Vektoren zu erzeugen:

Q = x @ W_q # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
K = x @ W_k # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
V = x @ W_v # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_v) -> (d_v,)

Dabei gilt:

  • W_q: Query-Gewichtsmatrix der Form (d_model, d_k)
  • W_k: Key-Gewichtsmatrix der Form (d_model, d_k)
  • W_v: Value-Gewichtsmatrix der Form (d_model, d_v)

Typischerweise gilt d_k = d_v = d_model für Single-Head-Attention (unterschiedliche Wahlmöglichkeiten mit Multi-Head-Attention betrachten wir später). Diese Gewichtsmatrizen sind gelernte Parameter — das Modell passt sie während des Trainings an, um herauszufinden, welche Projektionen für die Aufgabe am nützlichsten sind.

Wichtige Erkenntnis: Die Projektionsmatrizen sind der „lernbare" Teil von Self-Attention. Sie ermöglichen es dem Modell, unterschiedliche Ähnlichkeitsfunktionen für verschiedene Arten von Beziehungen zu lernen. Ein Attention-Head könnte lernen, sich auf syntaktische Struktur zu konzentrieren (Subjekt-Verb-Kongruenz), während ein anderer semantische Beziehungen lernt (Ähnlichkeit der Wortbedeutung). Das rohe Embedding kann dies nicht leisten, da es sich um eine einzige, feste Repräsentation handelt.

Warum drei separate Projektionen?

Eine naheliegende Frage ist: Warum nicht einfach die rohen Embeddings für alles verwenden? Die Antwort liegt in der Asymmetrie der Attention-Beziehungen.

Betrachten Sie den Satz: „The animal did not cross the street because it was too tired." Beim Verarbeiten von „it" muss das Modell feststellen, dass sich „it" auf „animal" bezieht (nicht auf „street"). Die Query für „it" muss kodieren „Ich bin ein Pronomen auf der Suche nach meinem Bezugswort", während der Key für „animal" kodieren muss „Ich bin ein Substantiv, das ein Bezugswort sein könnte". Das sind sehr unterschiedliche Rollen, die unterschiedliche Projektionen desselben Embedding-Raums erfordern.

Darüber hinaus kann sich das, was „animal" liefert, wenn ihm Aufmerksamkeit geschenkt wird (sein Value), von der Art unterscheiden, wie es sich präsentiert (sein Key). Der Value könnte reichhaltigen semantischen Inhalt über Tiere tragen, während der Key nur signalisieren muss: „Ich bin ein singuläres, belebtes Substantiv".

Self-Attention Schritt für Schritt berechnen

Kombinieren wir nun die QKV-Projektionen mit dem Dot-Product-Attention-Mechanismus aus Lektion 13. Die vollständige Self-Attention-Berechnung lautet:

  1. Eingaben durch W_q, W_k, W_v projizieren, um Q-, K-, V-Matrizen zu erhalten
  2. Attention-Scores berechnen: Q multipliziert mit K-transponiert
  3. Skalieren mit sqrt(d_k)
  4. Softmax anwenden, um die Attention-Gewichte zu erhalten
  5. Gewichte mit V multiplizieren, um die Ausgabe zu erhalten

In Matrixnotation lautet die berühmte Attention-Formel:

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V

Diese eine Zeile ist eine der folgenreichsten Gleichungen der modernen KI. Lassen Sie uns sie anhand von Code entschlüsseln.

Python
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 """Numerically stable softmax."""
 e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True))
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)


class SingleHeadSelfAttention:
 """
 Single-head self-attention mechanism implemented from scratch.

 This is the fundamental building block of the Transformer.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, d_k, d_v, seed=42):
 """
 Args:
 d_model: Input embedding dimension
 d_k: Query/Key projection dimension
 d_v: Value projection dimension
 """
 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))

 self.d_k = d_k
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale

 def forward(self, X):
 """
 Compute self-attention.

 Args:
 X: Input tensor of shape (seq_len, d_model)

 Returns:
 output: Attention output of shape (seq_len, d_v)
 weights: Attention weights of shape (seq_len, seq_len)
 """
 # Step 1: Project to Q, K, V
 Q = X @ self.W_q # (seq_len, d_k)
 K = X @ self.W_k # (seq_len, d_k)
 V = X @ self.W_v # (seq_len, d_v)

 # Step 2: Compute scaled dot-product scores
 scores = Q @ K.T # (seq_len, seq_len)
 scores = scores / np.sqrt(self.d_k)

 # Step 3: Softmax
 weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1) # (seq_len, seq_len)

 # Step 4: Weighted sum of values
 output = weights @ V # (seq_len, d_v)

 return output, weights

Was Q, K, V lernen zu repräsentieren

Während des Trainings werden die Gewichtsmatrizen W_q, W_k und W_v durch Gradientenabstieg optimiert. Aber was lernen sie tatsächlich?

Queries: „Wonach suche ich?"

Die Query-Projektion lernt, jedes Token in eine Repräsentation dessen zu transformieren, welche Information dieses Token aus dem Kontext benötigt. Zum Beispiel könnte die Query eines Verbs kodieren „Ich brauche ein Subjekt" oder „Ich brauche ein Objekt", während die Query eines Pronomens kodieren könnte „Ich brauche mein Bezugswort".

Keys: „Was biete ich an?"

Die Key-Projektion lernt, ein „durchsuchbares Etikett" für jedes Token zu erzeugen — eine Repräsentation dessen, welche Information dieses Token liefern kann. Der Key eines Substantivs könnte kodieren „Ich bin ein Subjekt-Kandidat" oder „Ich trage Entitätsinformation".

Values: „Welchen Inhalt trage ich?"

Die Value-Projektion bestimmt, welche Information tatsächlich weitergegeben wird, wenn einem Token Aufmerksamkeit geschenkt wird. Das ist häufig reichhaltiger und detaillierter als der Key. Während der Key sagt „Ich habe semantischen Inhalt über Tiere", trägt der Value die tatsächlichen semantischen Merkmale.

Profi-Tipp: Ein nützliches mentales Modell ist, dass Q und K das Routing bestimmen (wer mit wem spricht), während V den Inhalt bestimmt (was übertragen wird). Diese Trennung von Routing und Inhalt ist eine der zentralen Innovationen, die Transformer so leistungsstark machen. Es ähnelt der Funktionsweise eines Postsystems: Die Adresse (Key-Query-Abgleich) bestimmt, wohin ein Brief geht, aber die Adresse ist getrennt vom Inhalt des Briefs (Value).

Attention-Muster: Was das Modell lernt

Trainierte Transformer-Modelle entwickeln bemerkenswert interpretierbare Attention-Muster. Die Forschung hat mehrere gängige Muster identifiziert, die verschiedene Attention-Heads lernen:

Positionale Attention

Manche Heads lernen, auf benachbarte Token zu achten (lokaler Kontext), auf das vorherige Token oder das nächste Token. Diese erfassen lokale syntaktische Muster.

Syntaktische Attention

Manche Heads lernen grammatikalische Beziehungen: Subjekte richten ihre Aufmerksamkeit auf ihre Verben, Adjektive richten ihre Aufmerksamkeit auf die Substantive, die sie modifizieren.

Koreferenz-Attention

Manche Heads spezialisieren sich darauf, Pronomen ihren Bezugswörtern zuzuordnen: „it" richtet seine Aufmerksamkeit stark auf das Substantiv, auf das es sich bezieht.

Semantische Attention

Manche Heads richten ihre Aufmerksamkeit unabhängig von der Position auf semantisch verwandte Wörter und erfassen so Themen- und Bedeutungsbeziehungen.

Visualisieren wir verschiedene Arten von Attention-Mustern, die während des Trainings entstehen könnten.

Der Self-Attention-Berechnungsgraph

Verfolgen wir die Dimensionen bei jedem Schritt von Self-Attention, um ein vollständiges mentales Modell aufzubauen. Nehmen wir an, wir haben eine Sequenz von T Token mit Embedding-Dimension d_model:

Schritt Operation Eingabeform Ausgabeform
1 Q = X @ W_q (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
2 K = X @ W_k (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
3 V = X @ W_v (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_v) (T, d_v)
4 scores = Q @ K.T (T, d_k) @ (d_k, T) (T, T)
5 scores / sqrt(d_k) (T, T) (T, T)
6 weights = softmax(scores) (T, T) (T, T)
7 output = weights @ V (T, T) @ (T, d_v) (T, d_v)
Wichtig: Die Attention-Gewichtsmatrix aus Schritt 6 ist eine (T, T)-Matrix. Für eine Sequenz von 1000 Token ist das eine Matrix mit einer Million Elementen. Bei 4096 Token sind es fast 17 Millionen Elemente. Diese quadratische Skalierung mit der Sequenzlänge ist der primäre rechnerische Engpass der Transformer-Attention und der Grund, warum viel Forschung in effiziente Attention-Varianten geflossen ist.

Parameteranzahl und Rechenkosten

Quantifizieren wir die Ressourcen, die Self-Attention benötigt:

  • Parameter: Drei Gewichtsmatrizen, jede der Größe (d_model x d_k), insgesamt 3 * d_model * d_k Parameter. Für GPT-2 mit d_model = 768 und d_k = 64 pro Head sind das 3 * 768 * 64 = 147.456 Parameter pro Head.
  • Berechnung: Die dominierenden Kosten entstehen durch die (T, T)-Attention-Matrix. Bei einer Sequenzlänge T und d_k Dimensionen sind das O(T^2 * d_k) Operationen.
  • Speicher: Das Speichern der vollständigen (T, T)-Attention-Matrix erfordert O(T^2) Speicher.

Diese quadratische Skalierung ist der Grund, warum Standard-Transformer mit sehr langen Sequenzen zu kämpfen haben und warum Techniken wie FlashAttention, Sparse Attention und Linear Attention entwickelt wurden.

Wichtigste Erkenntnisse

  • Drei Projektionen, drei Rollen: Die Query fragt „was brauche ich?", der Key wirbt mit „was habe ich?", und der Value trägt „was ich dir geben werde." Die Trennung dieser Rollen ist essenziell.
  • Gelernte Projektionen ermöglichen flexible Attention: Unterschiedliche Gewichtsmatrizen W_q, W_k, W_v können lernen, unterschiedliche Arten von Beziehungen (syntaktisch, semantisch, positional) aus derselben Eingabe zu erfassen.
  • Die Attention-Formel: softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V berechnet Attention in einem einzigen eleganten Ausdruck, der vollständig differenzierbar und GPU-freundlich ist.
  • Quadratische Komplexität: Die T x T Attention-Matrix bedeutet, dass Rechen- und Speicherkosten quadratisch mit der Sequenzlänge wachsen — der primäre Engpass von Transformer-Modellen.
  • Interpretierbare Muster entstehen: Trainierte Attention-Heads entwickeln unterschiedliche, oft interpretierbare Spezialisierungen (syntaktisches Parsing, Koreferenzauflösung, positionale Attention).

Mécanisme d'auto-attention

Comment les projections Query, Key et Value transforment l'attention simple en puissant mécanisme d'auto-attention au cœur de chaque Transformer
50 min de lecture Exercices de code pratiques Intermédiaire-Avancé

De l'attention simple à l'auto-attention

Dans le Cours 13, nous avons implémenté l'attention par produit scalaire en utilisant les embeddings bruts à la fois comme vecteurs de requête et comme vecteurs clés. Bien que cela fonctionne, cela présente une limitation fondamentale : l'embedding de chaque token doit servir simultanément de « question » qu'il pose, de « réponse » qu'il fournit aux autres, et d'« information » qu'il transporte. C'est trop de rôles pour un seul vecteur.

L'auto-attention résout ce problème en introduisant trois projections apprises séparées qui transforment l'embedding de chaque token en trois rôles distincts :

  • Query (Q) : « Que suis-je en train de chercher ? » — représente l'information dont ce token a besoin
  • Key (K) : « Que contiens-je ? » — représente l'information que ce token offre
  • Value (V) : « Quelle information est-ce que je fournis réellement ? » — le contenu qui est agrégé
Analogie : La recherche en bibliothèque

Imaginez une bibliothèque où chaque livre possède une fiche de catalogue (Key) décrivant son contenu ainsi que le contenu réel du livre (Value). Lorsque vous arrivez avec une question de recherche (Query), vous comparez votre question à chaque fiche de catalogue. Les fiches qui correspondent le mieux vous indiquent quels livres lire. Vous lisez ensuite un mélange pondéré de ces livres, proportionnel à la qualité de correspondance de leurs fiches de catalogue avec votre question. L'auto-attention fonctionne de manière identique — Query, Key et Value ne sont que des « vues » différentes de chaque token, apprises pour remplir ces rôles spécifiques.

Les matrices de transformation QKV

Chaque embedding d'entrée x de dimension d_model est projeté à travers trois matrices de poids pour produire les vecteurs Query, Key et Value :

Q = x @ W_q # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
K = x @ W_k # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
V = x @ W_v # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_v) -> (d_v,)

Où :

  • W_q : Matrice de poids Query de forme (d_model, d_k)
  • W_k : Matrice de poids Key de forme (d_model, d_k)
  • W_v : Matrice de poids Value de forme (d_model, d_v)

En général, d_k = d_v = d_model pour l'attention à une seule tête (nous verrons des choix différents avec l'attention multi-têtes plus tard). Ces matrices de poids sont des paramètres appris — le modèle les ajuste pendant l'entraînement pour découvrir quelles projections sont les plus utiles pour la tâche.

Point clé : Les matrices de projection constituent la partie « apprenable » de l'auto-attention. Elles permettent au modèle d'apprendre des fonctions de similarité différentes pour différents types de relations. Une tête d'attention pourrait apprendre à se concentrer sur la structure syntaxique (accord sujet-verbe), tandis qu'une autre apprend des relations sémantiques (similarité de sens des mots). L'embedding brut ne peut pas faire cela car il s'agit d'une représentation unique et fixe.

Pourquoi trois projections séparées ?

Une question naturelle est : pourquoi ne pas simplement utiliser les embeddings bruts pour tout ? La réponse réside dans l'asymétrie des relations d'attention.

Considérez la phrase : « The animal did not cross the street because it was too tired. » Lors du traitement de « it », le modèle doit déterminer que « it » fait référence à « animal » (et non à « street »). La query pour « it » doit encoder « je suis un pronom qui cherche son antécédent », tandis que la key pour « animal » doit encoder « je suis un nom qui pourrait être un antécédent ». Ce sont des rôles très différents qui nécessitent des projections différentes du même espace d'embedding.

De plus, ce qu'« animal » fournit lorsqu'on lui accorde de l'attention (sa Value) peut être différent de la façon dont il s'annonce (sa Key). La Value peut porter un contenu sémantique riche sur les animaux, tandis que la Key n'a besoin que de signaler « je suis un nom singulier, animé ».

import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

d_v = 6 # value dimension

# Initialize QKV weight matrices (in practice, learned via training)
# Using Xavier/Glorot initialization
scale_init = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))
W_q = np.random.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale_init
W_k = np.random.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale_init
W_v = np.random.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale_init

print("=== QKV Projections ===\
")

print("W_q shape: {} (d_model x d_k)".format(W_q.shape))
print("W_k shape: {} (d_model x d_k)".format(W_k.shape))
print("W_v shape: {} (d_model x d_v)".format(W_v.shape))

# Project all tokens at once (matrix multiplication)
Q = X @ W_q # (n_tokens, d_k)
K = X @ W_k # (n_tokens, d_k)
V = X @ W_v # (n_tokens, d_v)

Q shape: {} (queries)".format(Q.shape))
print("K shape: {} (keys)".format(K.shape))
print("V shape: {} (values)".format(V.shape))

for i, tok in enumerate(tokens):

 k_norm = np.linalg.norm(K[i])

 # How different are Q and K for the same token?
 qk_cos = np.dot(Q[i], K[i][:d_k]) / (q_norm * k_norm + 1e-8)
 print(" '{}': |Q|={:.2f}, |K|={:.2f}, |V|={:.2f}, cos(Q,K)={:.3f}".format(
 tok, q_norm, k_norm, v_norm, qk_cos))

Notice: Q and K for the same token are NOT identical!")
print("The projections learn different 'views' of each token.")
print("cos(Q,K) varies per token - they encode different aspects.")

Calculer l'auto-attention étape par étape

Combinons maintenant les projections QKV avec le mécanisme d'attention par produit scalaire du Cours 13. Le calcul complet de l'auto-attention est le suivant :

  1. Projeter les entrées à travers W_q, W_k, W_v pour obtenir les matrices Q, K, V
  2. Calculer les scores d'attention : Q multiplié par K-transposée
  3. Mettre à l'échelle par sqrt(d_k)
  4. Appliquer softmax pour obtenir les poids d'attention
  5. Multiplier les poids par V pour obtenir la sortie

En notation matricielle, la célèbre formule de l'attention :

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V

Cette seule ligne est l'une des équations les plus déterminantes de l'IA moderne. Décortiquons-la avec du code.

Python
import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 """Numerically stable softmax."""
 e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True))
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)


class SingleHeadSelfAttention:
 """
 Single-head self-attention mechanism implemented from scratch.

 This is the fundamental building block of the Transformer.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, d_k, d_v, seed=42):
 """
 Args:
 d_model: Input embedding dimension
 d_k: Query/Key projection dimension
 d_v: Value projection dimension
 """
 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))

 self.d_k = d_k
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale

 def forward(self, X):
 """
 Compute self-attention.

 Args:
 X: Input tensor of shape (seq_len, d_model)

 Returns:
 output: Attention output of shape (seq_len, d_v)
 weights: Attention weights of shape (seq_len, seq_len)
 """
 # Step 1: Project to Q, K, V
 Q = X @ self.W_q # (seq_len, d_k)
 K = X @ self.W_k # (seq_len, d_k)
 V = X @ self.W_v # (seq_len, d_v)

 # Step 2: Compute scaled dot-product scores
 scores = Q @ K.T # (seq_len, seq_len)
 scores = scores / np.sqrt(self.d_k)

 # Step 3: Softmax
 weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1) # (seq_len, seq_len)

 # Step 4: Weighted sum of values
 output = weights @ V # (seq_len, d_v)

 return output, weights

Comprendre ce que Q, K, V apprennent à représenter

Pendant l'entraînement, les matrices de poids W_q, W_k et W_v sont optimisées par descente de gradient. Mais qu'apprennent-elles réellement ?

Queries : « Que suis-je en train de chercher ? »

La projection de query apprend à transformer chaque token en une représentation de l'information dont ce token a besoin dans le contexte. Par exemple, la query d'un verbe pourrait encoder « j'ai besoin d'un sujet » ou « j'ai besoin d'un complément d'objet », tandis que la query d'un pronom pourrait encoder « j'ai besoin de mon antécédent ».

Keys : « Que puis-je offrir ? »

La projection de key apprend à créer une « étiquette consultable » pour chaque token — une représentation de l'information que ce token peut fournir. La key d'un nom pourrait encoder « je suis un candidat sujet » ou « je porte une information d'entité ».

Values : « Quel contenu est-ce que je transporte ? »

La projection de value détermine quelle information est réellement transmise lorsqu'on accorde de l'attention à un token. Elle est souvent plus riche et plus détaillée que la key. Alors que la key dit « j'ai un contenu sémantique sur les animaux », la value porte les caractéristiques sémantiques réelles.

Astuce : Un modèle mental utile est de considérer que Q et K déterminent le routage (qui parle à qui), tandis que V détermine le contenu (ce qui est transmis). Cette séparation entre routage et contenu est l'une des innovations clés qui rendent les Transformers si puissants. C'est comparable au fonctionnement d'un système postal : l'adresse (la correspondance Key-Query) détermine où va une lettre, mais l'adresse est séparée du contenu de la lettre (la Value).

Schémas d'attention : ce que le modèle apprend

Les modèles Transformer entraînés développent des schémas d'attention remarquablement interprétables. Les recherches ont identifié plusieurs schémas courants que différentes têtes d'attention apprennent :

Attention positionnelle

Certaines têtes apprennent à porter attention aux tokens proches (contexte local), au token précédent, ou au token suivant. Elles capturent des schémas syntaxiques locaux.

Attention syntaxique

Certaines têtes apprennent des relations grammaticales : les sujets portent attention à leurs verbes, les adjectifs portent attention aux noms qu'ils qualifient.

Attention de coréférence

Certaines têtes se spécialisent dans la résolution des pronoms vers leurs antécédents : « it » porte fortement attention au nom auquel il fait référence.

Attention sémantique

Certaines têtes portent attention à des mots sémantiquement liés indépendamment de leur position, capturant des relations de sujet et de sens.

Visualisons différents types de schémas d'attention susceptibles d'émerger pendant l'entraînement.

Le graphe de calcul de l'auto-attention

Retraçons les dimensions à chaque étape de l'auto-attention pour construire un modèle mental complet. Supposons que nous ayons une séquence de T tokens avec une dimension d'embedding d_model :

Étape Opération Forme d'entrée Forme de sortie
1 Q = X @ W_q (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
2 K = X @ W_k (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
3 V = X @ W_v (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_v) (T, d_v)
4 scores = Q @ K.T (T, d_k) @ (d_k, T) (T, T)
5 scores / sqrt(d_k) (T, T) (T, T)
6 weights = softmax(scores) (T, T) (T, T)
7 output = weights @ V (T, T) @ (T, d_v) (T, d_v)
Important : La matrice de poids d'attention à l'étape 6 est une matrice (T, T). Pour une séquence de 1000 tokens, cela représente une matrice d'un million d'éléments. Pour 4096 tokens, cela représente près de 17 millions d'éléments. Cette mise à l'échelle quadratique avec la longueur de séquence est le principal goulot d'étranglement computationnel de l'attention des Transformers, et la raison pour laquelle de nombreuses recherches ont porté sur des variantes d'attention plus efficaces.

Nombre de paramètres et coût computationnel

Quantifions les ressources qu'exige l'auto-attention :

  • Paramètres : Trois matrices de poids, chacune de taille (d_model x d_k), totalisant 3 * d_model * d_k paramètres. Pour GPT-2 avec d_model = 768 et d_k = 64 par tête, cela représente 3 * 768 * 64 = 147 456 paramètres par tête.
  • Calcul : Le coût dominant est la matrice d'attention (T, T). Pour une longueur de séquence T et des dimensions d_k, cela représente O(T^2 * d_k) opérations.
  • Mémoire : Stocker la matrice d'attention complète (T, T) nécessite O(T^2) de mémoire.

Cette mise à l'échelle quadratique explique pourquoi les Transformers standards peinent avec les séquences très longues, et pourquoi des techniques comme FlashAttention, l'attention parcimonieuse (sparse attention) et l'attention linéaire ont été développées.

Points clés à retenir

  • Trois projections, trois rôles : la Query demande « de quoi ai-je besoin ? », la Key annonce « qu'est-ce que j'ai ? », et la Value transporte « ce que je vais te donner ». Séparer ces rôles est essentiel.
  • Les projections apprises permettent une attention flexible : différentes matrices de poids W_q, W_k, W_v peuvent apprendre à capturer différents types de relations (syntaxiques, sémantiques, positionnelles) à partir de la même entrée.
  • La formule de l'attention : softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V calcule l'attention en une seule expression élégante, entièrement différentiable et adaptée au GPU.
  • Complexité quadratique : la matrice d'attention T x T signifie que les coûts computationnels et mémoire croissent quadratiquement avec la longueur de séquence — le principal goulot d'étranglement des modèles Transformer.
  • Des schémas interprétables émergent : les têtes d'attention entraînées développent des spécialisations distinctes et souvent interprétables (analyse syntaxique, résolution de coréférence, attention positionnelle).

LEZIONE 14 Fase 3: Attenzione

Meccanismo di Auto-Attenzione (Self-Attention)

Come le proiezioni Query, Key e Value trasformano l'attenzione semplice nel potente meccanismo di self-attention al cuore di ogni Transformer
50 min di lettura Esercizi pratici di codice Intermedio-Avanzato

Dall'attenzione semplice alla self-attention

Nella Lezione 13, abbiamo implementato l'attenzione a prodotto scalare usando gli embedding grezzi sia come vettori di query sia come vettori chiave. Sebbene funzioni, presenta un limite fondamentale: l'embedding di ogni token deve fungere contemporaneamente da "domanda" che pone, da "risposta" che offre agli altri e da "informazione" che trasporta. Sono troppi ruoli per un singolo vettore.

La self-attention risolve questo problema introducendo tre proiezioni apprese separate che trasformano l'embedding di ogni token in tre ruoli distinti:

  • Query (Q): "Cosa sto cercando?" — rappresenta l'informazione di cui questo token ha bisogno
  • Key (K): "Cosa contengo?" — rappresenta l'informazione che questo token offre
  • Value (V): "Quale informazione fornisco effettivamente?" — il contenuto che viene aggregato
Analogia: La ricerca in biblioteca

Immagina una biblioteca in cui ogni libro ha una scheda di catalogo (Key) che ne descrive il contenuto e il vero e proprio contenuto del libro (Value). Quando entri con una domanda di ricerca (Query), confronti la tua domanda con ogni scheda di catalogo. Le schede che corrispondono meglio ti indicano quali libri leggere. Leggi poi una miscela ponderata di quei libri, proporzionale a quanto bene le loro schede di catalogo corrispondevano alla tua domanda. La self-attention funziona in modo identico — Query, Key e Value sono semplicemente "viste" diverse di ogni token, apprese per svolgere questi ruoli specifici.

Le matrici di trasformazione QKV

Ogni embedding di input x di dimensione d_model viene proiettato attraverso tre matrici di pesi per produrre i vettori Query, Key e Value:

Q = x @ W_q # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
K = x @ W_k # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
V = x @ W_v # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_v) -> (d_v,)

Dove:

  • W_q: matrice di pesi della Query, di forma (d_model, d_k)
  • W_k: matrice di pesi della Key, di forma (d_model, d_k)
  • W_v: matrice di pesi della Value, di forma (d_model, d_v)

Tipicamente, d_k = d_v = d_model per l'attenzione a singola testa (vedremo scelte diverse con la multi-head attention più avanti). Queste matrici di pesi sono parametri appresi — il modello le regola durante l'addestramento per scoprire quali proiezioni sono più utili per il compito.

Punto chiave: Le matrici di proiezione sono la parte "apprendibile" della self-attention. Consentono al modello di apprendere funzioni di similarità diverse per diversi tipi di relazioni. Una testa di attenzione potrebbe imparare a concentrarsi sulla struttura sintattica (accordo soggetto-verbo), mentre un'altra apprende relazioni semantiche (somiglianza di significato tra parole). L'embedding grezzo non può farlo perché è una rappresentazione singola e fissa.

Perché tre proiezioni separate?

Una domanda naturale è: perché non usare semplicemente gli embedding grezzi per tutto? La risposta risiede nell'asimmetria delle relazioni di attenzione.

Consideriamo la frase: "L'animale non ha attraversato la strada perché era troppo stanco." Quando elabora "era" (riferito all'animale), il modello deve determinare che il riferimento è "animale" (non "strada"). La query per il pronome deve codificare "sono un pronome/riferimento alla ricerca del mio antecedente", mentre la key per "animale" deve codificare "sono un sostantivo che potrebbe essere un antecedente". Questi sono ruoli molto diversi che richiedono proiezioni diverse dello stesso spazio di embedding.

Inoltre, ciò che "animale" fornisce quando viene attenzionato (il suo Value) potrebbe essere diverso da come si presenta (la sua Key). Il Value potrebbe trasportare un ricco contenuto semantico sugli animali, mentre la Key deve solo segnalare "sono un sostantivo singolare e animato".

Calcolare la self-attention passo dopo passo

Ora combiniamo le proiezioni QKV con il meccanismo di attenzione a prodotto scalare della Lezione 13. Il calcolo completo della self-attention è:

  1. Proietta gli input tramite W_q, W_k, W_v per ottenere le matrici Q, K, V
  2. Calcola i punteggi di attenzione: Q moltiplicato per K trasposta
  3. Scala per sqrt(d_k)
  4. Applica la softmax per ottenere i pesi di attenzione
  5. Moltiplica i pesi per V per ottenere l'output

In notazione matriciale, la famosa formula dell'attenzione:

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V

Questa singola riga è una delle equazioni più determinanti dell'IA moderna. Analizziamola con il codice.

import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 """Softmax numericamente stabile."""
 e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True))
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)


class SingleHeadSelfAttention:
 """
 Meccanismo di self-attention a singola testa implementato da zero.

 Questo è il blocco costitutivo fondamentale del Transformer.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, d_k, d_v, seed=42):
 """
 Args:
 d_model: Dimensione dell'embedding di input
 d_k: Dimensione della proiezione Query/Key
 d_v: Dimensione della proiezione Value
 """
 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))

 self.d_k = d_k
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale

 def forward(self, X):
 """
 Calcola la self-attention.

 Args:
 X: Tensore di input di forma (seq_len, d_model)

 Returns:
 output: Output dell'attenzione di forma (seq_len, d_v)
 weights: Pesi di attenzione di forma (seq_len, seq_len)
 """
 # Passo 1: Proietta su Q, K, V
 Q = X @ self.W_q # (seq_len, d_k)
 K = X @ self.W_k # (seq_len, d_k)
 V = X @ self.W_v # (seq_len, d_v)

 # Passo 2: Calcola i punteggi scaled dot-product
 scores = Q @ K.T # (seq_len, seq_len)
 scores = scores / np.sqrt(self.d_k)

 # Passo 3: Softmax
 weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1) # (seq_len, seq_len)

 # Passo 4: Somma pesata dei value
 output = weights @ V # (seq_len, d_v)

 return output, weights

Capire cosa apprendono a rappresentare Q, K, V

Durante l'addestramento, le matrici di pesi W_q, W_k e W_v vengono ottimizzate tramite discesa del gradiente. Ma cosa imparano effettivamente?

Query: "Cosa sto cercando?"

La proiezione della query apprende a trasformare ogni token in una rappresentazione di quale informazione quel token necessita dal contesto. Ad esempio, la query di un verbo potrebbe codificare "ho bisogno di un soggetto" o "ho bisogno di un oggetto", mentre la query di un pronome potrebbe codificare "ho bisogno del mio antecedente".

Key: "Cosa offro?"

La proiezione della key apprende a creare un'"etichetta ricercabile" per ogni token — una rappresentazione di quale informazione quel token può fornire. La key di un sostantivo potrebbe codificare "sono un candidato soggetto" o "porto informazioni su un'entità".

Value: "Quale contenuto trasporto?"

La proiezione del value determina quale informazione viene effettivamente trasmessa quando un token viene attenzionato. Questo è spesso più ricco e dettagliato della key. Mentre la key dice "ho contenuto semantico sugli animali", il value trasporta le caratteristiche semantiche effettive.

Consiglio pratico: Un modello mentale utile è che Q e K determinano l'instradamento (chi parla con chi), mentre V determina il contenuto (cosa viene trasmesso). Questa separazione tra instradamento e contenuto è una delle innovazioni chiave che rendono i Transformer così potenti. È simile a come funziona un sistema postale: l'indirizzo (la corrispondenza Key-Query) determina dove va una lettera, ma l'indirizzo è separato dal contenuto della lettera (Value).

Pattern di attenzione: cosa apprende il modello

I modelli Transformer addestrati sviluppano pattern di attenzione notevolmente interpretabili. La ricerca ha identificato diversi pattern comuni che le varie teste di attenzione apprendono:

Attenzione posizionale

Alcune teste imparano a concentrarsi sui token vicini (contesto locale), sul token precedente o sul token successivo. Questi catturano pattern sintattici locali.

Attenzione sintattica

Alcune teste apprendono relazioni grammaticali: i soggetti si concentrano sui loro verbi, gli aggettivi si concentrano sui sostantivi che modificano.

Attenzione correferenziale

Alcune teste si specializzano nel risolvere i pronomi ai loro antecedenti: "esso" si concentra fortemente sul sostantivo a cui si riferisce.

Attenzione semantica

Alcune teste si concentrano su parole semanticamente correlate indipendentemente dalla posizione, catturando relazioni di argomento e significato.

Il grafo computazionale della self-attention

Ripercorriamo le dimensioni a ogni passo della self-attention per costruire un modello mentale completo. Supponiamo di avere una sequenza di T token con dimensione di embedding d_model:

Passo Operazione Forma dell'input Forma dell'output
1 Q = X @ W_q (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
2 K = X @ W_k (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
3 V = X @ W_v (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_v) (T, d_v)
4 scores = Q @ K.T (T, d_k) @ (d_k, T) (T, T)
5 scores / sqrt(d_k) (T, T) (T, T)
6 weights = softmax(scores) (T, T) (T, T)
7 output = weights @ V (T, T) @ (T, d_v) (T, d_v)
Importante: La matrice dei pesi di attenzione al Passo 6 è una matrice (T, T). Per una sequenza di 1000 token, si tratta di una matrice con un milione di elementi. Per 4096 token, sono quasi 17 milioni di elementi. Questa scalabilità quadratica rispetto alla lunghezza della sequenza è il principale collo di bottiglia computazionale dell'attenzione nei Transformer, ed è il motivo per cui molta ricerca si è concentrata su varianti efficienti dell'attenzione.

Numero di parametri e costo computazionale

Quantifichiamo le risorse richieste dalla self-attention:

  • Parametri: tre matrici di pesi, ciascuna di dimensione (d_model x d_k), per un totale di 3 * d_model * d_k parametri. Per GPT-2 con d_model = 768 e d_k = 64 per testa, sono 3 * 768 * 64 = 147.456 parametri per testa.
  • Calcolo: il costo dominante è la matrice di attenzione (T, T). Per una lunghezza di sequenza T e dimensioni d_k, sono O(T^2 * d_k) operazioni.
  • Memoria: memorizzare l'intera matrice di attenzione (T, T) richiede O(T^2) memoria.

Questa scalabilità quadratica è il motivo per cui i Transformer standard faticano con sequenze molto lunghe e per cui sono state sviluppate tecniche come FlashAttention, l'attenzione sparsa e l'attenzione lineare.

Punti chiave da ricordare

  • Tre proiezioni, tre ruoli: la Query chiede "di cosa ho bisogno?", la Key pubblicizza "cosa ho da offrire?" e il Value trasporta "cosa ti darò". Separare questi ruoli è essenziale.
  • Le proiezioni apprese abilitano un'attenzione flessibile: matrici di pesi diverse W_q, W_k, W_v possono imparare a catturare diversi tipi di relazioni (sintattiche, semantiche, posizionali) dallo stesso input.
  • La formula dell'attenzione: softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V calcola l'attenzione in un'unica elegante espressione, completamente differenziabile e adatta alle GPU.
  • Complessità quadratica: la matrice di attenzione T x T comporta costi computazionali e di memoria che crescono in modo quadratico con la lunghezza della sequenza — il principale collo di bottiglia dei modelli Transformer.
  • Emergono pattern interpretabili: le teste di attenzione addestrate sviluppano specializzazioni distinte, spesso interpretabili (parsing sintattico, risoluzione della correferenza, attenzione posizionale).

يحل الانتباه الذاتي هذه المشكلة بإدخال ثلاثة إسقاطات مُتعلَّمة منفصلة تُحوّل تمثيل كل رمز إلى ثلاثة أدوار متمايزة:

  • Query (Q): "ما الذي أبحث عنه؟" — يمثّل المعلومة التي يحتاجها هذا الرمز
  • Key (K): "ما الذي أحتويه؟" — يمثّل المعلومة التي يقدّمها هذا الرمز
  • Value (V): "ما المعلومة التي أقدّمها فعليًا؟" — المحتوى الذي يتم تجميعه
تشبيه: البحث في المكتبة

تخيّل مكتبةً حيث تمتلك كل كتاب بطاقة فهرسة (Key) تصف محتواه، ومحتوى الكتاب الفعلي (Value). عندما تدخل ومعك سؤال بحثي (Query)، تقارن سؤالك بكل بطاقة فهرسة. تخبرك البطاقات التي تتطابق بشكل أفضل بالكتب التي ينبغي قراءتها. ثم تقرأ مزيجًا مرجّحًا من تلك الكتب متناسبًا مع مدى تطابق بطاقات الفهرسة الخاصة بها مع سؤالك. تعمل آلية الانتباه الذاتي بالطريقة نفسها — فـ Query وKey وValue ليست سوى "رؤى" مختلفة لكل رمز، تم تعلّمها لتخدم هذه الأدوار المحددة.

Q = x @ W_q # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)
K = x @ W_k # (d_model,) @ (d_model, d_k) -> (d_k,)

  • W_k: مصفوفة أوزان Key بالشكل (d_model, d_k)
  • W_v: مصفوفة أوزان Value بالشكل (d_model, d_v)

عادةً، d_k = d_v = d_model بالنسبة للانتباه أحادي الرأس (سنرى اختيارات مختلفة مع الانتباه متعدد الرؤوس لاحقًا). هذه المصفوفات هي معاملات متعلَّمة — يقوم النموذج بضبطها أثناء التدريب لاكتشاف أي الإسقاطات هي الأكثر فائدة للمهمة.

فكرة أساسية: مصفوفات الإسقاط هي الجزء "القابل للتعلّم" من الانتباه الذاتي. فهي تسمح للنموذج بتعلّم دوال تشابه مختلفة لأنواع مختلفة من العلاقات. قد يتعلّم أحد رؤوس الانتباه التركيز على البنية النحوية (توافق الفاعل والفعل)، بينما يتعلّم رأس آخر العلاقات الدلالية (تشابه معاني الكلمات). لا يستطيع التمثيل الخام القيام بذلك لأنه تمثيل واحد ثابت.

لماذا ثلاثة إسقاطات منفصلة؟

سؤال طبيعي يُطرح هنا: لماذا لا نستخدم التمثيلات الخام لكل شيء؟ تكمن الإجابة في عدم تناظر علاقات الانتباه.

تأمّل الجملة: "The animal did not cross the street because it was too tired." عند معالجة كلمة "it"، يحتاج النموذج إلى تحديد أن "it" تشير إلى "animal" (وليس "street"). يحتاج استعلام "it" إلى ترميز فكرة "أنا ضمير أبحث عن مرجعي"، بينما يحتاج مفتاح "animal" إلى ترميز فكرة "أنا اسم يمكن أن يكون مرجعًا". هذان دوران مختلفان تمامًا يتطلبان إسقاطات مختلفة لنفس فضاء التمثيلات.

علاوة على ذلك، ما تُقدّمه "animal" فعليًا عند الانتباه إليها (قيمتها Value) قد يختلف عن الطريقة التي تُعلن بها عن نفسها (مفتاحها Key). فقد تحمل Value محتوى دلاليًا غنيًا عن الحيوانات، بينما لا يحتاج Key إلا إلى الإشارة إلى "أنا اسم مفرد وحيّ".

حساب الانتباه الذاتي خطوة بخطوة

لنجمع الآن بين إسقاطات QKV وآلية انتباه الضرب النقطي من المحاضرة 13. حساب الانتباه الذاتي الكامل هو:

  1. إسقاط المدخلات عبر W_q وW_k وW_v للحصول على مصفوفات Q وK وV
  2. حساب درجات الانتباه: Q مضروبة في K المنقولة (transpose)
  3. القياس بالقسمة على sqrt(d_k)
  4. تطبيق softmax للحصول على أوزان الانتباه
  5. ضرب الأوزان في V للحصول على الناتج

بالتدوين المصفوفي، صيغة الانتباه الشهيرة:

Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V

هذا السطر الواحد هو من أكثر المعادلات تأثيرًا في الذكاء الاصطناعي الحديث. دعونا نفكّكه بالكود.

import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)

def softmax(x, axis=-1):
 """Numerically stable softmax."""
 e_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=axis, keepdims=True))
 return e_x / np.sum(e_x, axis=axis, keepdims=True)


class SingleHeadSelfAttention:
 """
 Single-head self-attention mechanism implemented from scratch.

 This is the fundamental building block of the Transformer.
 """

 def __init__(self, d_model, d_k, d_v, seed=42):
 """
 Args:
 d_model: Input embedding dimension
 d_k: Query/Key projection dimension
 d_v: Value projection dimension
 """
 rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
 scale = np.sqrt(2.0 / (d_model + d_k))

 self.d_k = d_k
 self.W_q = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_k = rng.randn(d_model, d_k) * scale
 self.W_v = rng.randn(d_model, d_v) * scale

 def forward(self, X):
 """
 Compute self-attention.

 Args:
 X: Input tensor of shape (seq_len, d_model)

 Returns:
 output: Attention output of shape (seq_len, d_v)
 weights: Attention weights of shape (seq_len, seq_len)
 """
 # Step 1: Project to Q, K, V
 Q = X @ self.W_q # (seq_len, d_k)
 K = X @ self.W_k # (seq_len, d_k)
 V = X @ self.W_v # (seq_len, d_v)

 # Step 2: Compute scaled dot-product scores
 scores = Q @ K.T # (seq_len, seq_len)
 scores = scores / np.sqrt(self.d_k)

 # Step 3: Softmax
 weights = softmax(scores, axis=-1) # (seq_len, seq_len)

 # Step 4: Weighted sum of values
 output = weights @ V # (seq_len, d_v)

 return output, weights

فهم ما تتعلّم Q وK وV تمثيله

أثناء التدريب، يتم تحسين مصفوفات الأوزان W_q وW_k وW_v عبر الانحدار التدرجي (gradient descent). لكن ما الذي تتعلّمه فعليًا؟

Queries: "ما الذي أبحث عنه؟"

يتعلّم إسقاط الاستعلام (query) تحويل كل رمز إلى تمثيل للمعلومة التي يحتاجها هذا الرمز من السياق. فعلى سبيل المثال، قد يرمّز استعلام فعل إلى "أحتاج إلى فاعل" أو "أحتاج إلى مفعول به"، بينما قد يرمّز استعلام ضمير إلى "أحتاج إلى مرجعي".

Keys: "ما الذي أقدّمه؟"

يتعلّم إسقاط المفتاح (key) إنشاء "تسمية قابلة للبحث" لكل رمز — تمثيل للمعلومة التي يمكن لهذا الرمز تقديمها. قد يرمّز مفتاح اسم إلى "أنا مرشح لأن أكون فاعلًا" أو "أحمل معلومات عن كيان".

Values: "أي محتوى أحمله؟"

يحدّد إسقاط القيمة (value) المعلومة التي تُنقل فعليًا عندما يُنتبه إلى رمز ما. وغالبًا ما يكون هذا أغنى وأكثر تفصيلًا من المفتاح. فبينما يقول المفتاح "لديّ محتوى دلالي عن الحيوانات"، تحمل القيمة السمات الدلالية الفعلية.

نصيحة احترافية: النموذج الذهني المفيد هو أن Q وK يحددان التوجيه (من يتحدث إلى من)، بينما تحدد V المحتوى (ما الذي يُنقل). هذا الفصل بين التوجيه والمحتوى هو أحد الابتكارات الرئيسية التي تجعل الـ Transformers بهذه القوة. يشبه الأمر عمل النظام البريدي: العنوان (تطابق Key-Query) يحدد وجهة الرسالة، لكن العنوان منفصل عن محتوى الرسالة (Value).

أنماط الانتباه: ما الذي يتعلّمه النموذج

تُطوّر نماذج Transformer المدربة أنماط انتباه قابلة للتفسير بشكل لافت. حددت الأبحاث عدة أنماط شائعة تتعلمها رؤوس انتباه مختلفة:

الانتباه الموضعي

تتعلّم بعض الرؤوس الانتباه إلى الرموز القريبة (السياق المحلي)، أو الرمز السابق، أو الرمز التالي. وهذه تلتقط الأنماط النحوية المحلية.

الانتباه النحوي

تتعلّم بعض الرؤوس علاقات نحوية: الفاعل ينتبه إلى فعله، والصفة تنتبه إلى الاسم الذي تصفه.

انتباه الإحالة المرجعية

تتخصص بعض الرؤوس في ربط الضمائر بمراجعها: تنتبه "it" بقوة إلى الاسم الذي تشير إليه.

الانتباه الدلالي

تنتبه بعض الرؤوس إلى الكلمات المرتبطة دلاليًا بغض النظر عن موضعها، فتلتقط علاقات الموضوع والمعنى.

مخطط حساب الانتباه الذاتي

لنتتبّع الأبعاد في كل خطوة من خطوات الانتباه الذاتي لبناء نموذج ذهني كامل. لنفترض أن لدينا تسلسلًا من T رموز ببُعد تمثيل d_model:

الخطوة العملية شكل الإدخال شكل الإخراج
1 Q = X @ W_q (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
2 K = X @ W_k (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_k) (T, d_k)
3 V = X @ W_v (T, d_model) @ (d_model, d_v) (T, d_v)
4 scores = Q @ K.T (T, d_k) @ (d_k, T) (T, T)
5 scores / sqrt(d_k) (T, T) (T, T)
6 weights = softmax(scores) (T, T) (T, T)
7 output = weights @ V (T, T) @ (T, d_v) (T, d_v)
مهم: مصفوفة أوزان الانتباه في الخطوة 6 هي مصفوفة بالشكل (T, T). بالنسبة لتسلسل من 1000 رمز، هذه مصفوفة من مليون عنصر. أما بالنسبة لـ 4096 رمزًا، فهي قرابة 17 مليون عنصر. هذا التوسع التربيعي مع طول التسلسل هو عنق الزجاجة الحسابي الأساسي في انتباه الـ Transformer، وهو السبب في أن أبحاثًا كثيرة انصبّت على أشكال فعّالة من الانتباه.

عدد المعاملات والتكلفة الحسابية

لنُحدّد كميًا الموارد التي يتطلبها الانتباه الذاتي:

  • المعاملات: ثلاث مصفوفات أوزان، كل منها بحجم (d_model x d_k)، بمجموع 3 * d_model * d_k معاملًا. بالنسبة لنموذج GPT-2 حيث d_model = 768 وd_k = 64 لكل رأس، فذلك يعني 3 * 768 * 64 = 147,456 معاملًا لكل رأس.
  • الحساب: التكلفة المهيمنة هي مصفوفة الانتباه (T, T). بالنسبة لطول تسلسل T وأبعاد d_k، فهذا يعادل O(T^2 * d_k) عملية.
  • الذاكرة: تخزين مصفوفة الانتباه الكاملة (T, T) يتطلب O(T^2) من الذاكرة.

هذا التوسع التربيعي هو سبب معاناة نماذج الـ Transformer القياسية مع التسلسلات الطويلة جدًا، وهو السبب في تطوير تقنيات مثل FlashAttention، والانتباه المتناثر (sparse attention)، والانتباه الخطي (linear attention).

أبرز النقاط

  • ثلاثة إسقاطات، ثلاثة أدوار: يسأل الـ Query "ما الذي أحتاجه؟"، ويُعلن الـ Key "ما الذي أملكه؟"، وتحمل الـ Value "ما الذي سأمنحك إياه." الفصل بين هذه الأدوار أمر أساسي.
  • الإسقاطات المتعلَّمة تتيح انتباهًا مرنًا: يمكن لمصفوفات الأوزان المختلفة W_q وW_k وW_v أن تتعلّم التقاط أنواع مختلفة من العلاقات (نحوية، دلالية، موضعية) من الإدخال نفسه.
  • صيغة الانتباه: softmax(Q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k)) @ V تحسب الانتباه في تعبير واحد أنيق قابل للاشتقاق التام وملائم لوحدات معالجة الرسوميات (GPU).
  • التعقيد التربيعي: مصفوفة الانتباه بالشكل T x T تعني أن التكاليف الحسابية وتكاليف الذاكرة تنمو تربيعيًا مع طول التسلسل — وهو عنق الزجاجة الأساسي لنماذج الـ Transformer.
  • ظهور أنماط قابلة للتفسير: تُطوّر رؤوس الانتباه المدرَّبة تخصصات متمايزة وقابلة للتفسير غالبًا (التحليل النحوي، حل الإحالة المرجعية، الانتباه الموضعي).
